title: Turn 3: deploy the token maker or hold for a protected Zada?

board.you: Turn 3, precombat main. Battlefield: Skirk Prospector, two Mountains and Goblin Burrows untapped (3 mana). Hand: Dragon Fodder, Brightstone Ritual, Zada, Hedron Grinder, Swiftfoot Boots, Mountain. Zada is castable next turn on curve (goldfish mean cast turn 4.35, 70% of games exactly turn 4).
board.table: Player 2 (Golgari midrange) holds two mana open with a deathtouch blocker. Player 3 (Azorius control, the table's known sweeper deck — assume it holds up 4+ mana for a wrath by turn 5-6) just tapped low for a draw spell. Player 4 (Selesnya tokens) has five tokens and an anthem and is currently the table's visible threat.

scenario.question: Do you cast Dragon Fodder now and develop wide — signaling the engine a turn early — or hold everything to land Zada with ritual or Boots protection?

branches.choice: Cast Dragon Fodder now, land Zada on schedule next turn
branches.line: Precombat: Dragon Fodder ('Create two 1/1 red Goblin creature tokens'), play the Mountain, pass with Prospector plus two tokens. Turn 4: cast Zada (goldfish: 70% of games do exactly this) and pass, holding Brightstone Ritual.
branches.signals: Two 1/1s next to a Prospector read as chump blockers against the Golgari deck, not an engine — the Selesnya board keeps drawing the table's attention. Zada on turn 4 with no cantrip shown looks like a mediocre 3/3.
branches.coalition_risk: Low this turn. The token deck at five bodies plus anthem is the lightning rod; nobody wastes a wrath on three Goblins.
branches.coaching: This is the line the deck is built for. Goldfish mean bodies on turn 3 is only 2.36 — Dragon Fodder now puts you above curve exactly when it's cheapest to do so, and 'early token maker drawn' averages turn 3.18, so this is the scripted tempo. Every body you add multiplies the engine: verified stack 001 shows four Goblins turning one Crimson Wisps into five cards, and each body also grows Brightstone Ritual ('Add {R} for each Goblin on the battlefield') for the turn you actually go off. Holding tokens in hand makes Zada, the Ritual, and the future cantrip all worse at once.

branches.choice: Hold everything; pass with three mana up
branches.line: Play the Mountain, pass with all mana open, representing interaction. Turn 4: cast Zada with Brightstone Ritual held as an instant-speed mana burst for a follow-up.
branches.signals: Passing with full mana open from a mono-red deck that has shown one Prospector reads as a bluff or a slow hand — Golgari may probe with an attack, and the Azorius player books you as low priority.
branches.coalition_risk: Medium. An unexplained hold from the red deck invites testing, and you fall behind the token deck's board while gaining nothing — Brightstone Ritual counts Goblins on the battlefield, so with one Goblin out it adds almost nothing.
branches.coaching: You're holding a ritual whose value you refuse to build. Yes, Brightstone Ritual is an instant so you can legally hold it for any priority window, but the card scales with the exact board you're declining to make. You keep Zada on the same schedule as the aggressive line while shrinking every payoff attached to her. This line only makes sense if you're representing removal you don't have — a bluff that costs you real tempo.

citations.quote: A player may cast an instant spell any time they have priority. A player may cast a noninstant spell during their main phase any time they have priority and the stack is empty.

branches.line: Turn 3: Dragon Fodder. Turn 4: Swiftfoot Boots plus a land. Turn 5: Zada. Turn 6: equip ({1}) and fire a cantrip with hexproof protection.
branches.signals: Boots cast before the commander telegraphs 'my commander must survive to matter' — experienced tables pre-answer Zada the moment she's cast, or hold exile removal for the equip window.
branches.coalition_risk: Low early, high late: by the time the protected engine turns on, you're past the point where the table forgives it, and the Azorius wrath window (4+ mana held turns 5-6) arrives before your engine does.
branches.coaching: The math says this is too slow. 'Zada online with a cantrip drawn' already averages turn 5.27 and happens by turn 6 in only 49.6% of games — pushing Zada to turn 5 pushes the engine to turn 6-7, where your land-drop rate has fallen to 54% and the sweeper deck has had two full turns of mana held up. Boots are how you protect Zada after she's proven she must die, not a precondition for casting her. Protection you pay for before anyone has shown a threat is tempo donated to the table.

recommendation.choice: Cast Dragon Fodder now, land Zada on schedule next turn
recommendation.rationale: Every payoff in this hand — Zada's copies (stack 001: bodies equal extra cards), Brightstone Ritual (mana per Goblin), even the eventual wide attack — is denominated in Goblins on the battlefield. Two 1/1 tokens on turn 3 carry near-zero threat signal at a table watching a five-token Selesnya board, so you buy the engine's fuel at the exact moment it's free. The goldfish curve (2.36 bodies turn 3, Zada turn 4.35, engine turn 5.27) is the deck's winning script; both holding lines delay the script without buying real protection.
